why: Replacing E1 with a real short trailing-fragment example made the scorer avoid keeping tiny trailing fragments (small positive changes in the ≤3 and ≤5 bins), but the model compensated by introducing more internal single-word splits and moving cuts closer to heads in longer pieces (negative changes in ≤7, ≤10, ≤99). The worst-moved pairs illustrate this side-effect (new one-word segments like “they”, “medication”, “upright”).
lesson: When adding an example to discourage very-short trailing fragments, ensure the change is localized so it does not induce extra internal one-word splits or shift cuts toward heads in longer pieces.
